head: bf3b6d2344cb523bd51a09459a1dcc1fb0dad15b
classification_reasons: Spec is not tight by the article's own bar: it touches sdlc.yaml risk_list item 'auth' end to end, and Flagged concern 3 explicitly accepts a residual gap in the heuristic parser rather than closing it outright.

Blast radius is wide: shell_guard.py's decide() runs on every Bash/PowerShell call in every phase, by hand and in CI, plus a second layer (sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite) added to plugin/ci/settings.ci.json, template/.claude/settings.json and plugin/ci/run_phase.py's ci_settings_file.

No existing test exercises a Bash/PowerShell write to a guardrail or locked test file today -- that bypass is exactly the intent's finding -- so the new behavior is not already covered by current tests; the plan correctly orders reproducing-tests-first but the coverage does not pre-exist.
attempted: Intent: compared spec.md/plan.md against intent.md's proposed outcome (every instance of the authz-by-tool-route pattern fixed, each proven by a test, an eval case for the class). The design still finds the second instance (test_file_lock.py), still plans both eval cases, and now also adds a sandbox write-deny layer as a second control named by the owner's x-sandbox decision (docs/reviews/2026-09-28-playbook-vs-framework/target-design.md, T29, verified present and worded as cited). No scope drift from intent.

Spec and plan: read the owner's 19-item fix-requests.json against the rewritten spec.md/plan.md item by item. All three Flagged concerns now literally start with 'decided' and each names what the acceptance/decision rests on (risk acceptance records in status.yaml; secrets_check.py out-of-scope rationale; the sandbox layer closing the heuristic's residual). Verified the single defect the prior adversarial round escalated on -- plan.md/spec.md citing a nonexistent `evals/check.py` -- is fully corrected: both Order of work step 9 and the Proof section now use `python plugin/evals/run.py --fixture --dry-run --case "<folder>"`, consistent with spec.md Acceptance. Checked plan.md's 'Files that change' lists files in the order plan.md's own Order of work touches them, and that the diff (evidence/diff-b.patch) touches only changes/0002.../{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**} -- no source files in this phase, as required (plan.md is produced by a read-only run).

Proof: cross-checked the design's load-bearing factual claims directly against the code rather than trusting the prose -- plugin/hooks/hooks.json's actual matcher wiring (plan_sync on two if-gated entries, production_gate ungated on Bash|PowerShell, panel_blind on Read|Grep|Bash|PowerShell|Write|Edit|MultiEdit) matches spec.md Design's 'Today' paragraph exactly; protected_paths.py exports protected_patterns/_check_one/REASON and test_file_lock.py exports locked_change_id/is_locked/test_path_patterns/REASON exactly as shell_guard.py is planned to import; production_gate.py exports command_parts/chain_parts as public functions, supporting the 'reuse, don't move' decision; plugin/scan/route.py:468 does route an unbounded finding to change_type 'feature'; plugin/gate/checks.py:1666 builds the eval dir from `{status.id}-{status.slug}` exactly, confirming the eval case must be named 0002-security-authz-the-guardrail-self-protec (not 0006-...) for gate (e)'s lesson_and_eval check, and that 0002-intent-skill-shape already exists (confirming the `--case "0002-*"` ambiguity named in the spec); plugin/ci/run_phase.py:695 and :2142 import protected_paths and test_file_lock exactly as cited; template/.claude/settings.json carries `Bash(git *)` plus three `{{..._RULE}}` placeholders, not `Bash(python *)` and friends, exactly as the corrected Design/Requirements now state (a fact the prior draft had wrong); plugin/skills/security-baseline/check.py's DANGEROUS patterns do match `eval(`, `exec(`, `shell=True` literally, supporting the Acceptance item about evasion-case test literals. No fabricated or unverifiable citation found. Phase (b) produces no toolchain logs by design (none expected: plan.md says tests are still to be written in phase (c)); evidence/ contains only the run/evidence records appropriate to a design-only phase.

Blast radius: shell_guard.py is new surface running on every Bash/PowerShell call across every phase (by hand and CI); the sandbox block is new surface in ci_settings_file, read by every CI phase job. Checked that plugin/gate/checks.py and plugin/skills/security-baseline/check.py's existing imports of protected_paths/test_file_lock are plain function imports unaffected by adding a third caller (shell_guard.py), matching the plan's 'no change to checks.py' claim. Confirmed sdlc.yaml risk_list's 'auth' is the only item implicated; no data-migration, money-movement or production-config path touched.

Policies: security-baseline rule 1 (authorization not inferred from tool route) is the requirement itself, correctly sourced; rule 6 (no new dependency) is honored -- shell_guard.py is specified to reuse re/shlex and production_gate's own helpers, nothing new; rule 8 (risk-list flagging) correctly fires and is correctly closed with an owner-recorded acceptance, not a self-granted one. coding-standards rule 2 (reuse) and rule 4 (no weakening existing tests) are both explicitly addressed in Requirements/Acceptance. UX and data-conventions are correctly marked not applicable (no screen, no schema).

Tests: no test code exists yet (phase (b) is design-only); evaluated whether the planned test shape (reproducing Bash/PowerShell-bypass tests written and seen to fail before the fix, direct unit tests of shell_write_targets and its negative list, a hooks.json wiring test, a ci_settings_file test, two --dry-run-validated eval cases) would actually prove the fix and not merely assert the plan's own wording -- the order (fail first, then fix, then re-run) matches intent's constraint and the shape is concrete enough (named test functions, named idiom classes, a specific hook-log assertion shape borrowed from evals/cases/0005-hooks-loaded, which was read and confirmed to exist in that shape) that phase (c) has no ambiguity about what 'passing' means. No existing test is touched by this diff; plan.md explicitly keeps protected_paths.py, test_file_lock.py, production_gate.py and _common.py unmodified, which is itself the fix for the prior round's test-breaking 'shared helper' approach.
